title: Classical ML theory I | Fine-tuning
objectives: Explain core algorithms and their trade-offs at whiteboard depth. Know when and how to fine-tune, and when not to. Checkpoint 2 on Day 7.
exercise: QLoRA-fine-tune a small open model (3–8B, free Colab/T4-class GPU) to classify transaction descriptions into categories. Compare it with your Week 5 prompt baseline on the same held-out set.
resources: Chip Huyen, Machine Learning Interviews (free online)
Unsloth Fine-tuning LLMs Guide and LoRA Hyperparameters Guide
Hugging Face LLM Course (includes RL/GRPO chapter)

cards.q: Why does L1 produce sparse coefficients?
choices: The L1 ball has corners on the axes, so the optimum often lands where some coefficients are exactly 0
cards.explain: L2's round ball shrinks all weights but rarely to exactly zero.

cards.q: Training error low, validation error high. Diagnosis and fix?
choices: High variance (overfitting): more data, regularisation, simpler model

cards.q: Increasing the regularisation strength λ typically…
Spot the leak: you standardise features using the mean/std of the full dataset, then do 5-fold CV.
choices: Validation-fold statistics leak into training; fit the scaler inside each fold (pipeline)
Standardisation is not allowed with CV

cards.q: With many correlated features, which tends to keep groups of them (shrinking together)?
Logistic regression coefficient 0.7 on a binary feature. The odds multiply by what factor when it's 1 vs 0? (2 dp)
cards.explain: e^0.7 ≈ 2.01, so the odds roughly double.

cards.q: Logistic regression is fit by…
Logistic regression models…
choices: Log-odds of the positive class as a linear function of features
The probability as a linear function

cards.q: A model is 'well calibrated' when…
choices: Among cases predicted at 20%, about 20% are positive

cards.q: Perfectly separable training data in unregularised logistic regression causes…
Bagging vs boosting: which primarily reduces variance and which primarily reduces bias?
choices: Bagging reduces variance; boosting reduces bias
Bagging reduces bias; boosting reduces variance

cards.q: Random forests add what on top of bagging?
choices: A random subset of features at each split, decorrelating trees

cards.q: Each new tree in gradient boosting fits…
choices: The negative gradient of the loss (residuals for squared error) of the current ensemble

cards.q: Lowering the learning rate (shrinkage) in XGBoost usually requires…
choices: More trees, often giving better generalisation

cards.q: Why do tree ensembles often beat neural networks on tabular data?
choices: They handle heterogeneous features, missing values and non-linear thresholds well with little tuning
Neural nets can't use tabular data

cards.q: The fraud rate is 0.1%. Why is ROC-AUC misleading, and what do you report instead?
cards.answer: ROC uses the false-positive rate, whose denominator is the huge negative class. A tiny FPR can still mean thousands of false alarms versus a few frauds, so ROC-AUC looks great while precision is poor. Report PR-AUC / average precision, precision and recall at the operating threshold, and cost-weighted metrics (fraud $ caught vs review cost).
rubric: High AUC can coexist with poor precision

cards.q: A fraud model flags 200 transactions; 50 are fraud. There were 100 frauds in total. What is the recall in %?
Same model: precision 25%, recall 50%. F1? (decimal, 3 dp)
With 0.1% positives, a model predicting 'not fraud' for everything has accuracy…
How should you pick the fraud classification threshold?
choices: From business costs: expected fraud loss avoided vs review cost/customer friction, on a validation set

cards.q: Your model lacks knowledge of last month's policies. Fine-tune or RAG?
cards.explain: Knowledge that changes belongs in retrieval; fine-tuning is for behaviour, format and style.

cards.q: Order the usual escalation ladder for improving an LLM application.
items: Fine-tuning for behaviour, format or cost

cards.q: Good reason TO fine-tune?
choices: A small model must match a large model's output format and style on a narrow task at lower cost/latency

cards.q: Before fine-tuning, what must exist?
choices: An eval set and a strong prompt baseline to beat

cards.q: Distillation for LLMs typically means…
choices: Training a smaller model on a larger model's outputs for a task

cards.q: A 4096×4096 weight with rank-16 LoRA: how many trainable parameters?
LoRA's update to a frozen weight W is…
choices: W + (α/r)·B·A with low-rank A (r×k) and B (d×r)

cards.q: Why is B initialised to zero in LoRA?
choices: So the adapter starts as a no-op and training begins from the base model's behaviour

cards.q: Practical advantage of LoRA adapters in serving?
choices: Many small task adapters can share one base model and be swapped or merged
They remove the need for the base model

cards.q: Applying LoRA to all linear layers (attention + MLP) rather than only Q/V usually…
choices: Improves quality at modest extra cost

cards.q: In QLoRA, what is quantised and what stays in higher precision?
choices: The frozen base weights are 4-bit (NF4); LoRA adapters and computation use 16-bit

cards.q: Main benefit of QLoRA over LoRA?
choices: Much lower GPU memory, so larger models fit on a single small GPU

cards.q: Unsloth's suggested starting learning rate for LoRA/QLoRA? (e.g. 0.0002)
If a well-tuned LoRA fails on your task, will full fine-tuning likely rescue it?
choices: Rarely: revisit the data and task framing first

cards.q: Sign of overfitting in an SFT run?
choices: Training loss keeps falling while validation loss rises and eval outputs get repetitive

cards.q: Which needs preference pairs, and which needs a verifiable reward function?
choices: DPO needs preference pairs; GRPO needs a (verifiable) reward function
GRPO needs pairs; DPO needs rewards

cards.q: GRPO estimates advantages by…
choices: Sampling a group of responses per prompt and comparing each reward to the group's mean (no value network)

cards.q: Good task for GRPO-style RL?
choices: Math or SQL generation where answers can be checked automatically

cards.q: Catastrophic forgetting means…
choices: Fine-tuning degrades capabilities the model had before (general skills)

cards.q: How should you evaluate a fine-tune?
choices: Against the base model and the prompt baseline on the same held-out task eval, plus a general-capability regression check
Ask the fine-tuned model if it improved
